policy_name: Massachusetts H 4885 (Firearm Laws), Section 148
question: Beyond the establishment of the special legislative commission, what specific measures or requirements are outlined in this section for ensuring the investigation and study of emerging firearm technologies?
answer_low_temp:
1. The special legislative commission is tasked with investigating and studying the status, feasibility, and utility of emerging firearm technologies, including personalized firearm technology and microstamp technology (Section 148d).
2. The study includes a review of existing and developing personalized firearm and microstamp technologies and any legal or constitutional issues relating to such technologies (Section 148d(i)).
3. The commission is required to investigate the accuracy, effectiveness, and utility of personalized firearm and microstamp technologies (Section 148d(ii)).
4. The commission is to evaluate the commercial availability of personalized firearm and microstamp technologies, both in the production of new firearms and modification of existing firearms (Section 148d(iii)).
5. The commission is to evaluate the feasibility and utility of a personalized firearm technology tax incentive program (Section 148d(iv)).
6. The commission is to evaluate the risks associated with the use of a digital firearm manufacturing code for machine learning and artificial intelligence (Section 148d(v)).
7. The commission is to investigate the cost and impacts associated with requiring the use of personalized firearm or microstamp technologies in the commonwealth (Section 148d(vi)).
8. The commission is to submit a report of its study and recommendations, together with any legislative recommendations, to the clerks of the house of representatives and the senate no later than March 1, 2025 (Section 148e).

Sources:
- Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 140, Section 148 (https://malegislature.gov/Laws/GeneralLaws/PartI/TitleXII/Chapter140/Section148)
